book.title: Career and Technical Education Grade 7 Student Textbook
book.subject: cte

title: Selecting chickens and feed sources
competency: Apply chicken selection criteria and list feed sources.

keywords.def: To remove weak or unwanted birds from the flock.

en.text: Select hens that hatch and mother well, chicks that grow fast, and birds that resist disease. Cull poor growers, dwarf birds and surplus cocks. Hatching eggs should be average size, with a good uncracked shell and a broad bottom and sharper tip. Day-old chicks should be healthy and keen to eat.

screens.title: Pick an egg
screens.ask: Which egg is best for hatching?
opts: Average size, clean shell, no cracks
screens.after: Average-sized eggs with good, uncracked shells hatch best.

screens.title: 3.4.3 Chicken selection criteria
table: Hens that protect chicks from predators
Keep fast growers; cull poor growers and dwarfs
Average size, good shell, broad bottom, sharp tip
Good body, no leg or eye deformity, keen to eat
Breed from birds that survive outbreaks

screens.title: Key words
defs: To remove weak or unwanted birds from the flock.

screens.text: Which hatching egg should you choose?
opts: Average size with a good, uncracked shell
screens.ans: Average size with a good, uncracked shell
screens.why: Average size, good shell, clear shape.

screens.text: A farmer should keep dwarf birds and poor growers.
Tap the signs of a good day-old chick.
screens.why: Healthy chicks are strong and eager to eat.

screens.text: Some of Almaz's birds survived a disease outbreak. Which should she breed from?
opts: New birds from an unknown market
screens.why: Breeding from survivors selects for disease resistance.

en.text: Egg production depends on feed. Chicken feed is mostly by-products of home food and agro-industries: household cooking waste, cereals and by-products, roots and tubers, oilseeds, trees and shrubs, animal proteins and commercially prepared feed.

screens.title: Fewer eggs
screens.ask: Your hens lay fewer eggs when you feed them less. Why?
screens.after: There is a clear link between feed and egg production.

screens.title: 3.4.4 Feed sources
paras: Egg production is clearly linked to feed and nutrients.
Most feeds are by-products of home food processing and agro-industries.

screens.why: The book says there is a clear relationship.

screens.title: Feed or not?
screens.why: All but plastic belong to the book's feed groups.
screens.clue: Can a chicken safely eat it?

screens.text: Commercially prepared feed is one feed source for chickens.
screens.why: It is on the book's list.

screens.text: A family has maize, kitchen leftovers and some termites the hens find. Which book feed groups do they have?
opts: Cereals, household waste and animal proteins
screens.ans: Cereals, household waste and animal proteins
screens.why: Maize is a cereal, leftovers are household waste, and termites are animal protein.
screens.clue: Match each feed to a group.

opts: Hens with good hatching and mothering behaviour
Hens that never sit on eggs
test.ans: Hens with good hatching and mothering behaviour

test.text: Household cooking waste can feed chickens.

opts: A broader bottom and a sharper tip
test.ans: A broader bottom and a sharper tip

test.text: Surplus cocks should always be kept.
test.why: Surplus cocks at slaughter age should be culled.

test.text: Wheat bran belongs to which feed group?
